title: The presheaf of isomorphism classes and its canonical fppf sheafification
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] within [def-weil-size-convention] and $\mathcal F$ a category fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A presentation of its presheaf of isomorphism classes consists of a set-valued presheaf $P$ and a functor $c:\mathcal F\to\operatorname{disc}(P)$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ whose map on isomorphism classes in every fibre over $T$ is bijective. Here $\operatorname{disc}(P)$ is the discrete fibred category of the presheaf, as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; thus $P(T)$ is exactly $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal F(T))/\cong$ and $c$ is its quotient map, compatibly with restriction. Its fppf isomorphism-class sheaf is the sheafification $Q=P^\#$ with unit $\eta:P\to Q$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. Equivalently, it is a sheaf $Q$ with $\eta$ such that composition with $\eta$ bijects $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Z)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Z)$ for every fppf sheaf $Z$. These data determine the sheaf and unit up to unique compatible isomorphism. The canonical map $\mathcal F\to Q$ is $c$ followed by $\operatorname{disc}(\eta)$. Whenever Mathlib's sheafification functor is supplied, take its actual value on $P$ and its actual adjunction unit, which satisfy this universal property.
